mutations.why: The whole point of finding 1. With the fallback unreachable, a push that cannot authenticate goes straight back to reporting 'failed' - which is the pre-fix behaviour that made finish-sprint.js exit 1 on every run on a Git-for-Windows host. Proves the fallback is what produces the deleted verdict, not some incidental property of the stub runner.
mutations.label: deleteBranch falls back to gh when git push cannot authenticate

mutations.why: Finding 2. Restoring the throw is exactly the pre-fix behaviour: a re-run after a partial failure died at the one step that had already succeeded, rather than retrying the one that had not. Isolates the idempotence from the resume path, which is tested separately.
mutations.label: markMerged is idempotent when the entry is already merged

mutations.why: The resume path is what makes idempotence useful: without it main() still refuses when the local branch is gone, so the remote can never be cleaned up by re-running. Making the branch unreachable restores the hole v0.3-s3 fell into.
mutations.label: main finishes the remote side when a partial run already deleted the local branch
mutations.expectRed: expected the remote delete to be retried

mutations.why: Finding 3. Silencing the comparison restores the assumption that the operator is on the trunk - the assumption that wrote v0.3-s3's STATUS.md flip onto an unrelated follow-up branch. The warning is the whole deliverable of that finding, so a test that passes without it would be testing nothing.
mutations.label: main warns which branch received the STATUS.md edit when it is not the trunk
